assessments.reasoning: Section 5.4.3.4 at pp.90–91 separates the runtime branches for legal Erase operands classified as variables. A declared fixed-size array resets each dependent variable to the standard initial value of the declared element type. A resizable array receives an empty array with the same element type.

challenge.method: Use the runtime detail on p.91 in addition to the overview on p.90. Compare an array held through Variant, a With block variable, a param array, and the other allowed expression classifications.
challenge.results: The two declared array branches explicitly provide the two outcomes. Variant has separate validity and mismatch logic. With block and param array exclusions constrain legality, and property/function cases do not control the declared-variable finding.

limitations: This judgment applies to the exact May 20, 2025 MS-VBAL revision 2.4. The publisher currently lists a later edition. Its requirements and behavior of any Office host are outside this review.
The exact claim does not specify memory deallocation, storage representation, or the concrete initial value for any element type.
